chimo.titulo_seo: Chimo, Cabo Corrientes: how to get there, what's there
chimo.descripcion_seo: Chimo is a fishing village of 280 people in Cabo Corrientes, 30 km from Puerto Vallarta. How to get there by boat or dirt road, and what is there.
chimo.hero_texto: A fishing village in Cabo Corrientes, at the southern end of Banderas Bay. Two hundred and eighty people and a beach that is nearly always empty.

secciones.titulo: Two hundred and eighty people and thirty kilometres of coast
parrafos: Chimo is a locality in the municipality of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco. About 280 people live here year-round, though the number rises in fishing season. It sits roughly 30 kilometres south of Puerto Vallarta along the coastline, and no paved road reaches it.

The day starts early. The boats go out before dawn and come back mid-morning with octopus, which is what the village lives on. The pier has been half-built for more than twenty years, so everything is landed on the beach by hand. There is a health post, though rarely a doctor.
The rest is the ocean. You hear it all day, and on moonless nights you hear it more.

hay_no_hay.titulo: What there is and what there isn't
hay_no_hay.intro: We would rather tell you now than have you find out on arrival.

gente.texto: This section will carry portraits and names of the people of the village: who takes you out in the boat, who cooks, who walks you up to the waterfalls. It is the one thing no other house on this coast can copy, which is why we would rather do it properly than quickly.

items.texto: The most visited village on the south shore. Same water, far more people.
A waterfall and horseback rides. Written up as the most untouched village in Mexico.
A small beach reachable only by sea.
First stop on the corridor, with beach restaurants.
Heavier surf, and a lighthouse built in 1902.
A bay between cliffs, known for its oysters. A shrimp boat that sank in 1920 is dived here.
An open 12 km beach with a sea turtle camp running since 2005.
The municipal seat at 1,085 m, five to ten degrees cooler. Panela cheese, coffee, honey and raicilla.

items: Cash in pesos. There is no ATM.
Any medication you need. There is no pharmacy.
Closed shoes if you plan to walk to the waterfalls.
A dry bag if you are taking gear out on the boat.

experiencias_pagina.descripcion_seo: Whales December 8 to March 23, Cabo Corrientes waterfalls, octopus fishing, kayaks and macaws. Each one with its season and who runs it.
experiencias_pagina.hero_texto: Things here have a season. The whales arrive on December 8. The waterfalls run full when it rains. Octopus comes out year-round, before dawn.
dia: The fishermen's boat leaves. If you are going, you are up before that.
Breakfast on the terrace with whatever came in.
Kayak to the next cove, before the wind comes up.
Lunch at one of the village kitchens.
Pool, hammock, or the walk to the lookout.
You hear the ocean and nothing else.

items.titulo: You are in the jungle, and the jungle has wildlife
parrafos: Chimo sits between the ocean and the hills, and that is exactly what makes it what it is. It also means insects get in, and now and then a scorpion. The house is treated and checked, but it is a house in the jungle, not a hotel room in a city.

If anyone in your group is allergic to a scorpion sting, tell us when you book. This matters: the village health post keeps emergency injections, but there is rarely a doctor on site, and we would much rather know beforehand than at midnight.

items.titulo: How we look after the house while you are here
parrafos: Housekeeping comes on the third day of your stay, without you having to ask. If you stay longer, we repeat it.
The house has security and a backup generator, and it is pet friendly: if you are bringing a dog, tell us the size so we can get everything ready.

alimentos.titulo: From the wave to the pan
alimentos.intro: The fishermen leave before first light and come back with the day's catch. What reaches the table is up to you.

items.texto: Included in your stay. We are still refining the menu, so if you have any dietary restriction, tell us and we will sort it out.
Ordered in advance and cooked at the house. Fish and seafood from the day's catch when the sea allows it.
Send us your list and we shop in Vallarta or El Tuito so you arrive to a full fridge. There is no supermarket in Chimo.

publico.titulo: People who come so that nothing happens
publico.texto: The house rents whole, so it makes no difference whether you are two or four. This is what comes up most among the people who write to us.

faq.titulo: What people ask before they come

items.p: How many people live in Chimo, Jalisco?
items.r: About 280. It is a locality in the municipality of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, and the number ranges between 180 and 300 depending on the fishing season and whether nearby ranches are counted.

items.p: How do you get to Chimo from Puerto Vallarta?
items.r: Three ways. By boat, about 2 hours 30 minutes from Puerto Vallarta. By panga from Boca de Tomatlán, roughly 40 minutes from the airport. Or overland via El Tuito, with about 3 hours of dirt road. There is no paved road to the village.

items.p: How far is Chimo from Puerto Vallarta?
items.r: About 30 kilometres south along the coastline, in the municipality of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco.

items.p: When can you see whales in Chimo?
items.r: The official humpback whale watching season in Banderas Bay runs December 8 to March 23, per the dates published in Mexico's federal gazette. Operators need a permit and a certification course.

items.p: Is there an ATM, pharmacy or supermarket in Chimo?
items.r: No. There is a health post, though rarely a doctor on site, and beach restaurants. Bring cash in pesos and any medication you need.

items.p: Does Villa Chimo have Wi-Fi and power?
items.r: Yes. The house has Wi-Fi, air conditioning and a backup power generator.

items.p: Are there scorpions or wildlife in Chimo?
items.r: It is a jungle area, so insects get in and now and then a scorpion. The house is treated and checked. If anyone in your group is allergic to a scorpion sting, tell us when you book.
Fishing. The catch sold is mainly octopus and fish. The village pier has been unfinished for more than twenty years, which limits the activity.

items.p: How much does Villa Chimo cost?
items.r: 150 US dollars per night plus taxes, for the whole house, up to 4 guests. There are discounts by the week, from 15 nights, and by the month.
